Literature question for a global sensitivity study. Unknown black-box function y = f(x1,...,x5), inputs continuous and independent, uniform in [-1,1]. Budget: exactly 64 function evaluations, no more. Goal: for each input, estimate (a) first-order variance-based sensitivity index (fraction of Var(y) explained by that input alone) and (b) total-order index (fraction of Var(y) in which the input takes part, alone or via interactions). Question: which methods give both numbers with 64 experiments, and which do you recommend, with concrete settings (e.g. Sobol/Saltelli design with N and second-order terms, Sobol' pick-freeze with sample size, polynomial chaos or Gaussian-process surrogate with Sobol index post-processing, Morris screening, HDMR, etc.) and the expected accuracy at this budget. Please quote the papers you rely on (authors, year, title) and give one sentence per method found. Keep the answer concise.

**Required deliverables / acceptance criteria:**
(1) List of methods found, one sentence each. (2) Your recommendation with exact settings for 64 evaluations (sample design, how many points per block, estimators, and how to handle the budget). (3) Papers quoted: authors, year, title.
